label: input token i during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter i as an input in the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It fires on every original-phase i (precision 1.0 on dev) at any position and for any L. Activation is fairly uniform (median 0.58, max 0.77). It tends to be highest for an i at the last original position, just before <DEL>, and lower for a repeated i. It does not fire on the <DEL> step. When i is fed back during the copy phase it barely fires, mostly weakly (about 0.15 of max) and only when i was orig(0) and is re-input at recall_idx 1. It almost never fires on other tokens; there are a few weak hits on m.

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says activation 'tends to be highest for an i at the last original position, just before <DEL>'. On test, an original-phase i at to_go==0 holds 15.3% of active steps but only 11.5% of the top activation quartile, so it is under-represented among the strongest activations. The real peak is at t==0: an i at t==0 is 15.3% of active steps but 61% of the top quartile and 0% of the other three quartiles (mass recall 0.179 vs recall 0.153). The dev profile shows the same thing: mass share by t falls from 0.179 at t=0 to 0.028 at t=8, and in the misses rendering the t=0 i's sit at about 0.88 of max. So activation is highest for i as the FIRST token and declines with later positions (an i at t>=4 is 38% of active steps but only 19% of the top quartile).

The core detector holds. On test, (phase==0)&(in_tok==i) has 0 inactive predicted steps, and the 1592 active steps it misses carry only 0.3% of activation mass. No systematic class of misses or false positives remains.

The copy-phase claim checks out. Copy-phase i fires rarely (an i input in the copy phase is 1.4% of active steps on test), mostly about 0.14-0.18 of max, and mostly at recall_idx 1 when orig(0)==i. Only about 7% of those re-inputs fire, so adding them to the predicate lowers F1 (0.931).

The claim that a repeated i fires lower holds weakly: in_first==0 is 9.2% of active steps but 4.5% of the top quartile. The weak hits on m are confirmed, and there are also scattered weak hits on the digit 1 at the last original position (noise).
